Construction staking

Construction staking is the process of marking on the ground where the features on a design drawing are to be built: building corners, road centrelines, utility runs and grade points.

It happens in stages. Rough staking sets out the general layout before earthwork. Finish staking follows grading and sets precise offsets for foundations and utilities. Each stage is tied back to the same control network so the whole site stays consistent.

Most disputes on a construction site about whether something is in the right place come down to whether the staking was tied to control or set by tape from an assumed point.
